findings.quoted_text: Contractor shall also perform any additional services [CLIENT_NAME] reasonably requests during the Term at no additional charge.
[CLIENT_NAME] may request unlimited revisions until [CLIENT_NAME] is fully satisfied with each Deliverable.
Either party may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice, subject to payment of fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date.
Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
Requests outside that scope are handled as part of the Services.
Contractor shall also perform any additional services [CLIENT_NAME] reasonably requests during the Term at no additional charge.
findings.explanation: The clause obliges the contractor to do any extra work the client asks for without extra compensation, exposing the freelancer to unlimited additional workload and no payment for it.
findings.suggested_change: Limit additional services to those agreed in writing with a fee, e.g., "Contractor shall perform additional services only upon a written change order signed by both parties and compensated at the rates set forth in Schedule X."

findings.quoted_text: [CLIENT_NAME] may request unlimited revisions until [CLIENT_NAME] is fully satisfied with each Deliverable.
findings.explanation: Allows the client to demand endless changes, causing the freelancer to invest unlimited time and resources without additional payment, potentially delaying project completion.
findings.suggested_change: Cap the number of revision rounds per Deliverable and charge for extras, e.g., "Client may request up to two rounds of revisions per Deliverable; additional revisions shall be billed at $[RATE] per hour."

findings.quoted_text: Either party may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice, subject to payment of fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date.
findings.explanation: The client can end the agreement on short notice, leaving the contractor with unrecovered costs for work in progress and no compensation for the disruption.
findings.suggested_change: Add a termination fee for client‑initiated convenience termination, e.g., "If Client terminates for convenience, Client shall pay Contractor a termination fee equal to 30% of the remaining scheduled fees."

findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: A 30‑day payment period can strain cash flow, and the client may withhold payment during a 15‑day dispute window, further delaying receipt of funds.
findings.suggested_change: Shorten payment terms and increase late‑payment interest, e.g., "Invoices shall be payable Net 15; any undisputed portion shall be paid within 15 days and disputed amounts shall be paid in full within 30 days. Late payments will accrue interest at 1.5% per month."

findings.explanation: You must provide any number of revisions at no extra cost, which can lead to endless work cycles and erode profitability.
findings.suggested_change: Limit revisions to a reasonable number (e.g., 2‑3 rounds) and specify that additional revisions will be billed at an agreed hourly rate.

findings.quoted_text: Requests outside that scope are handled as part of the Services.
findings.explanation: The clause allows the client to request work beyond the agreed scope without a clear mechanism for extra compensation, exposing you to unpaid additional effort.
findings.suggested_change: Add language that any out‑of‑scope work requires a written change order and will be billed separately at the agreed rates.

findings.explanation: Payment is due 30 days after invoice, and the interest for late payment is low, so you may face cash‑flow issues if the client delays payment.
findings.suggested_change: Negotiate a shorter payment period (e.g., Net 15) and a higher late‑payment interest rate (e.g., 1.5‑2% per month) or include a penalty for overdue invoices.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

I hope you are well. Before signing, I would like to suggest a few adjustments to the agreement:
- The relevant clause obliges the contractor to perform any additional services requested by the client at no additional charge, which could lead to unlimited extra work without compensation. I propose that additional services be performed only upon a written change order signed by both parties and compensated at the rates set out in the schedule.
- The relevant clause allows the client to request unlimited revisions until fully satisfied, which may result in unbounded time spent on changes. I suggest capping revisions to two rounds per deliverable, with any additional revisions billed at the agreed hourly rate.
- The relevant clause permits either party to terminate for convenience with 20 days’ written notice, leaving the contractor exposed to unrecovered costs. I recommend adding a termination fee for client‑initiated convenience termination equal to 30 % of the remaining scheduled fees.
- The relevant clause sets payment terms at Net 30 and a 1 % per month late‑payment interest, which may strain cash flow. I propose shortening payment terms to Net 15, requiring undisputed amounts to be paid within 15 days and applying a 1.5 % per month interest on late payments.
- The relevant clause states an unlimited revision allowance at no extra cost, exposing the contractor to endless work cycles. I suggest limiting revisions to a reasonable number (e.g., two to three rounds) and billing any additional revisions at the agreed hourly rate.
- The relevant clause treats requests outside the defined scope as part of the services, which could result in unpaid extra work. I propose that any out‑of‑scope work require a written change order and be billed separately at the agreed rates.

Thank you for your consideration.

Best regards.
